summary:
The SC-130 reorder is sound. The spike proved it, and the code at PoolWatch.ps1:329-336 and :384-397 bears out the design's claims about which flag combinations are reachable. The problems are in the case-exactness work and in the checks that are supposed to make it hold.

**Case-exactness is mostly built already.** HEAD's PoolWatch.ps1 already compares tags case-exactly: Read-Mark uses `-ccontains` at :207 and Tag() uses `-ceq` at :242. There is also no WC* family to convert, because :66 names nine WC tags. The real risks are elsewhere:
- **The architecture rule misses the one site that matters.** It cannot see Tag()'s `$_.tag -ceq $name`, so a change back to `-eq` passes it.
- **The P-004 fixture can pass falsely.** It only catches that change if the case variant comes before the real tag in the mark's tags array. The committed SL-095 logs do put Ntff ahead of NtfF.
- **Get-Net's `[ordered]@{}` keys by tag name and ignores case.** It will merge the NtfF and Ntff columns as soon as the later reader slice adds Ntff to $NetTags. Nothing in this slice tests that.
- **P-004's live half cannot catch a misspelled new tag.** It skips any name that is absent from the live table, so a typo is skipped too.

**PoolWatchCases still writes under the engine's TEMP.** The design leaves PoolWatchCases rooting its fixtures in GetTempPath(), which is C:\WINDOWS\TEMP for the engine. It does so on a build-check measurement that never says which TEMP it ran under, against lesson #391 and the fitness rule rationale.

**Unproven preconditions:**
- **Same workload:** holds. Invoke-Protocol :609 runs all five full scans with the same root and the same arguments.
- **Warm SizeProbe repeat (SC-230):** if the probe pass churns NtfF, the protocol needs a new arm. That arm has to exist before the person's one-shot Restart session, but the design does not order SC-230 before session 1.

**Smaller defects:**
- One P-003 check contradicts the output the design requires: the guard reason itself contains "MiB".
- The 'then interrupted before its /settled mark' suffix is wrong in two reachable cases.
- The check that every hand-off id was dispositioned is vacuous for six of the ids.
- The reading rule's 'WC columns' leave out three leak tags.
- The cited Q&A thread also reports the same mechanism reaching 24.4 GB, which the design record omits.

findings.evidence: tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1:242 `function Tag(...) ... Where-Object { $_.tag -ceq $name })[0]` is the only lookup Live/Get-Net use. The rule as already appended is at .taad/fitness.yaml:1176-1178. The design's corpus check lists only `$WatchedTags -contains`, `-in $NetTags` and `-like 'WC*'`. Per CC-007, the corpus must include the variants already in the repo. Settle by running Fitness on a scratch copy with :242 edited to `-eq`: it reports 0 hits today.
findings.fix:
Add these patterns, and add the matching wrong and right lines to the corpus:
- `\.tag\s+-i?(eq|ne|like|notlike|match|notmatch|in|notin|contains|notcontains)\b`
- `\btag\s+-i?(eq|ne|like|notlike|match|notmatch)\b`
- `\$_\[0\]\s+-i?(eq|ne|like|match|in|notin)\b`
The corpus must include `Where-Object { $_.tag -eq $name }` and `Where-Object tag -eq $t` as wrong, and `$_.tag -ceq $name` as right.

findings.claim: The P-004 fixture half can pass with the very bug it exists to catch. Tag() returns `[0]` of the matching entries. If a lookup regresses to case-folding while the fixture lists NtfF before Ntff, the first match is still NtfF, so the NtfF column comes out right and the check passes. The design does not say what order the fixture's tags go in. Real data puts the variant first: the committed build-2026-10-05 marks hold "Ntff" ahead of "NtfF" in the tags array of every line.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:242 returns `@(...)[0]`. In docs/design/SL-095-runs/build-2026-10-05/marks.jsonl line 1, the tag order runs WCse, FMwi, WCce, WCfc, WCsc, Ntff, WCrb, SeAt, FMfn, NtFC, Toke, NtfF, ...; build-marks.jsonl has the same order on all 7 lines.
findings.fix: P-004's fixture must put Ntff before NtfF, and NtxF before NtxI, in both marks, with different live counts. It then asserts the NtfF column equals the NtfF delta. Also mutate Tag() to `-eq` in a scratch copy once and confirm P-004 goes red.

findings.claim: Get-Net builds its result as `[ordered]@{}` and keys it by tag name (`$net[$t] = ...` for each tag in $NetTags). PowerShell's ordered dictionaries, like hashtables, ignore case in their keys. This slice leaves $NetTags without Ntff or NtxF, so neither the rule nor P-004 can see this seam. The design files 'a -Report reader for the 14 new tags' to the measurement-preparation slice. The natural way to write that reader is to add Ntff and NtxF to $NetTags. At that point `$net['Ntff']` overwrites `$net['NtfF']`, and the NtfF column the outcome-C reading decides on silently shows Ntff's value, which moves the opposite way. The design says, in general terms, to convert tag-keyed @{} to Ordinal dictionaries, but no case checks that it happened here.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:515-516. To settle it, run `pwsh -NoProfile -Command '$n=[ordered]@{}; $n["NtfF"]=1; $n["Ntff"]=2; $n.Count'`, and the same under powershell.exe. The expected result is 1 (recalled, not run here).
findings.fix: Build $net as `New-Object System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary ([StringComparer]::Ordinal)` now. In P-004's fixture half, load Get-Net with the parser, call it with a $NetTags that includes both NtfF and Ntff, and assert the two values are separate.

findings.claim: The first P-004 live assertion reads: 'each of the 14 new names that is present case-exactly in the live table is in the mark'. The names come from the script's own $WatchedTags, loaded by the parser ('never use a copied list'). A misspelled entry such as 'NtFS', 'NtfO' for Ntf0, or 'Mmre' is then absent from the live table, gets skipped, and P-004 passes. The person's one-shot Restart session would then be recorded without that tag. Recording these tags before that session is the stated reason they are in this slice (lesson #344). The condition 'present in the live table' cannot tell a typo from a tag that is genuinely absent, such as Ntce on a quiet boot.
findings.evidence: This is the design's P-004 live half and its rationale for STEP 2. The names are easy to mistype: Ntf0 has a zero, and NtFs, FSim, MmSm, MmRe and Ntce all mix case.
findings.fix:
Give P-004 its own literal list of the 14 expected names as the oracle, and assert:
- each is `-ccontains` in the parsed $WatchedTags;
- each name that is always live on an NTFS boot (NtfF, Ntff, NtxI, NtxF, Ntfo, MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, File) is in the live mark.
Read the live table before calling Read-Mark, because tags appear in the table but do not disappear from it.

findings.claim: The design leaves PoolWatchCases.ps1 rooting its fixtures in GetTempPath() and removing them with `Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`. It justifies this with 'the build check measured all 9 fixture cases at exit 0, and a measurement outranks the lesson'. But that measurement records no TEMP value. The sc130 spike explicitly ran under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp and did not run C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. Lesson #391, which was measured, names PoolWatchCases.ps1 as red under the engine's TEMP. The fitness rationale at .taad/fitness.yaml:1164-1167 says this Remove-Item throws a terminating Win32Exception(5) that SilentlyContinue does not suppress. All of the new P-003 and P-004 checks run through this script, and their check commands use no TEMP wrapper. The slice's own repro avoids the problem with Get-ScratchParent.
findings.evidence: PoolWatchCases.ps1:99, :120, :242, :258, :336, :352. Lesson #391 lists PoolWatchCases.ps1 as still unfixed. tests/bugs/SL-099-GuardStopSurvivesInterrupt.Tests.ps1:41-49 holds Get-ScratchParent. Q-220 says engine runs set TEMP=TMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. To settle it, run `-Case P-003` through a wrapper that prints GetTempPath() under the engine's TEMP.
findings.fix: Copy the repro's Get-ScratchParent into PoolWatchCases.ps1 and use it at :99, :242 and :336, so every fixture is rooted in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when TEMP is under the Windows folder. That is three lines, it needs no separate slice, and it makes this slice's own new checks dependable at build and validate.

findings.claim:
The design reads its leak-against-cache question from the slope across the five full scans F1-F5. Four of the preconditions behind that are must-verify, and the design does not say what breaks if one fails. One of them, SC-230, can force a new arm type in Invoke-Protocol, yet filed_for_later does not put SC-230 before the person's session 1. Precondition by precondition:
(1) Same workload: settled now, and it holds. :609 passes the same root, exe-full type and a null hook to every F arm.
(2) F1 is cold: Defender, the indexer and SysMain can warm parts of C: in the up to 30 minutes before R0 and the 20-minute I0. That only understates F1.
(3) The cache survives from F1 to F2-F5: if it is evicted, F2-F5 show positive NtfF. That reads as a leak, Q-178 (3) fails wrongly, and the reading points at the Q-183 scanner path.
(4) A warm SizeProbe repeat nets about 0 NtfF (SC-230): if file-FCB churn makes NtfF non-zero, the deciding column cannot decide. The design's own remedy is a listing-only repeat arm, which has to exist before the person's one-shot Restart, or that Restart is spent.
findings.evidence: The design's cross_domain_transfer invariants and its decidable_disagreements entry (would_force_resynthesis: true). filed_for_later puts only the measurement-preparation slice 'before session 1'. SC-230 is listed as a separate slice with no ordering.
findings.fix: In filed_for_later and in the record, make SC-230 (a Sandbox run on created files) a precondition of session 1. Make the measurement-preparation slice carry the listing-only repeat arm whenever SC-230 comes out no-go. In the record, mark precondition (1) as holds and cite :609.

findings.claim: STEP 1 asks the builder to make every tag comparison case-exact and says 'the WC family becomes -clike WC*'. HEAD is already case-exact: Read-Mark uses `-ccontains` at :207 and Tag() uses `-ceq` at :242. There is no WC family either, because :66 names nine WC tags. The 'marks.jsonl tags array' contract describes marks as holding 'WC*' and 'a WC entry is any tag beginning case-exactly with WC'. A builder following it could add a family filter and change what marks record. P-004's live assertions 2-4 cannot fail when the reading is a -ccontains filter over distinct 4-byte names. Record item (i), whether 0feac0e folded case, can be answered by grep now. Also, the committed build-2026-10-05 marks were written with a list that included SeAt and NtFC, and they already hold Ntff.
findings.fix: Replace STEP 1 with 'keep :207 and :242 as they are; add no WC* family; append the 14 names to the named list at :66'. Drop P-004 live assertions 2-4. Answer record item (i) from :207 and :242, and note that any reader of the committed build-2026-10-05 logs must be case-exact.

findings.claim: For P-003 arm (c) the check requires 'no MiB figure on that arm's line', and the contract's error case says 'No figure is printed'. But the line must carry the guard's reason, and Invoke-ExeArm writes that reason as 'available N MB, pool +N MiB over <arm>/before'. So the correct output fails the check as written, and a builder who makes it pass has to weaken it.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:354. The design's arm (c) expectation and its contract error_cases.
findings.fix: Assert instead that arm (c)'s guard line contains 'its net at the stop is unread' and does not contain 'from /before to /exit'.

findings.claim:
The suffix '; then interrupted before its /settled mark' is always printed, and it is wrong in two reachable cases:
- variant (c): the interrupt came before /exit;
- the /settled mark was written at :365, then a terminating error or Ctrl+C hit during the report read (:366-380) before the arm line was written at :381. ConvertFrom-Json on a torn report from the killed exe is one way. The finally then sets interrupted while /settled exists.
Separately, the not-interrupted guard branch adds 'mark <arm>/settled is missing' but drops HEAD's field checks on /settled (:469-470). A /settled with null tags would then go unreported.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:362-382, the finally at :389-396, and HEAD's field loop at :466-471.
findings.fix: Take the suffix wording from the marks that exist: 'before its /exit mark' when /exit is absent, 'before its /settled mark' when only /settled is absent, otherwise 'after its /settled mark'. In the not-interrupted branch, run the four field checks on /settled.

findings.claim: The hand-off check only tests that each id string appears somewhere in the new record. The record is required to cite the spikes, whose evidence is written as M0-M4 and N1/N2 marks and control arms, and the repro's X1/X2 arms. So M2, M3, M4, N1, N2 and X2 are satisfied without any disposition being written. The check also ignores three hand-off items that have no id: the slice's steps 3 to 5, calibrating the store-relative cancel trigger, and whether a ScanArm-like rig returns. The case's own 'why' names exactly this silent drop-out.
findings.fix: Have the record hold a disposition table, one row per hand-off item, and have the check match `(?m)^\| <id> \| (settled here|carried|dropped)` for each of the 14 ids and the 3 named items.

quote.text: SC-128 redoes the design for outcome C. It receives, by finding id: R3-1 and R4-1 (the settle gate, and its per-pool

findings.claim: Record item (d) reads Q-178 (1) as 'the WC columns are +0 on every arm', and (3) as 'NtfF and the WC columns'. -Report's WC columns are only WCsc, WCfc and WCri. The leak tags WCse, WCss and WCfn are recorded in every mark (:66) but appear in no column. Read from the -Report table, the 0-WC* claim would leave out half of the leak tags SL-095 named.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:66-67. In the SL-095 scratch decision 1, the leak tags are WCsc, WCse, WCss, WCfc, WCri, WCfn and FMwi.
findings.fix: In the record, name the full WC leak set the reading uses, and either add WCse/WCss/WCfn to the reader work filed for the measurement-preparation slice or state that they are read from marks.jsonl.

findings.claim: The design cites Microsoft Q&A 5966064 as outside support for 'designed caching'. The source does back the cold-path figure of about 1 KB per path. It also reports that the same tags reached 24.4 GB combined pool (10,786 MB nonpaged) after 47.41 hours on a 32 GB PC, cleared only by a reboot. That is the magnitude of this project's own tens-of-GB report. Release under deep pressure has been shown only in a 4 GB Sandbox (SC-231), so the cited source is at least as much evidence that this mechanism can produce Q-188's growth without giving it back. That bears on the 'no scanner change' decision, which the design itself rates expensive to reverse.
findings.evidence: The page at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5966064/windows-11-25h2-kernel-pool-leak-fmfn-and-file-all says: 'combined pool reached 24.4 GB after 47.41 hours: 10,786 MB nonpaged and 13,626 MB paged ... 3,000 first-time opens cost about 1 KB of pool per path'.
findings.fix: In record item (b), quote the 24.4 GB figure next to the 1 KB-per-path figure. Say plainly that the source does not show the state being given back at that size, and that Q-188 may be this mechanism with the app's cold scans as a contributor.

findings.claim: The reading rule says that if the 6 GiB guard stops F1, 'F2-F5 are then read only among themselves'. But a guard-stopped F1 has warmed only part of C:. F2 then pays the cold cost of the rest and is not a warm repeat. Reading F2 alongside F3-F5 counts that cold remainder as per-pass growth. The predicted cold cost of 3-4.4 GiB is close enough to the 6 GiB guard for this to happen.
findings.evidence: PoolWatch.ps1:63 (6 GiB per arm) and the SL-095 design doc :211-216 (3 to 4.4 GiB predicted, unmeasured).
findings.fix: In record item (d), say that after a guard-stopped F1, F2 is partly cold and is excluded from the repeat set. Only F3-F5 are read as repeats.

dimensions_checked.result:
Four findings:
- M5: PoolWatchCases under the engine's TEMP, justified by a measurement whose TEMP was never recorded.
- M6: the must-verify preconditions, with SC-230 not ordered before session 1. 'Same workload' is settled as holding (:609).
- m1: STEP 1 assumes HEAD folds case. It does not (:207, :242).
- m6: the cited Q&A also reports 24.4 GB.
The recalled PowerShell case-folding claims were checked: about_Switch says it is case-insensitive by default, and a reference page says comparison operators are case-insensitive unless c-prefixed.

m3: the suffix wording is wrong when the interrupt came before /exit or after /settled was written, and the not-interrupted guard branch drops the /settled field checks. m7: a guard-stopped F1 leaves F2 partly cold. Checked and correct: the design's claim that guardAtStart plus interrupted cannot happen (:329-336 returns before the try).

M3: Get-Net's `[ordered]@{}` keyed by tag name will merge NtfF and Ntff the moment the filed reader slice adds Ntff to $NetTags. That invariant holds only by remembering, and no case in this slice reaches it.

m1: STEP 1 converts code that is already case-exact, and three of P-004's live assertions are vacuous by construction. The rest of the scope is proportionate. Recording 21 named tags rather than the whole table, writing the record as a doc rather than a judge, and adding P-003 arms are all justified.
m2: arm (c)'s 'no MiB figure' check contradicts the guard reason the line must contain, which is written at :354. m5: 'the WC columns' leave WCse, WCss and WCfn out of the 0-WC* reading.

Traced the guard and interrupt paths through Invoke-ExeArm (:350-397). A guard stop followed by an interrupt in the settle wait produces exitCode -1 with killed false, which is fixture X1. Kill followed by an interrupt before /exit produces variant (c). The CIM-failure route is the same. The only wrong output is the suffix wording (m3). Get-Net's null return is handled by the 'unread' wording.

None. The design keeps answered decisions Q-178, Q-183, Q-184 and Q-185 intact. It self-rescoped, using the lessons, after the build check asked a person to rescope. SC-129 (Y3) is triggered by the design's own 0-WC* claim and then filed to the measurement-preparation slice, so it is recorded rather than lost. No ScanArm InternalsVisibleTo line remains in src. The stack line still naming ScanArm is stale but harmless.

M1: the architecture rule cannot see the variable-RHS comparison in Tag(), simplified Where-Object syntax, `switch`, or `$_[0]` comparisons (CC-007). The new strings respect fitness.yaml:1093-1100 (no verdict words) and stay ASCII. tests/bugs/SL-098-ReturnValueCorpus.json covers only RuleCases.ps1, so no census row is needed.

M2: the P-004 fixture passes falsely unless the variant comes before NtfF, and the real committed logs do order it first. M4: the live half cannot catch a misspelled new tag. m4: the hand-off-id check is vacuous for M2, M3, M4, N1, N2 and X2 and skips three items. The acceptance repro and the P-003 arms otherwise cover the SC-130 branches.
None. Nothing is elevated, nothing new is written outside the run folders and scratch, and the pool and handle reads stay unelevated through NtQuerySystemInformation as today.
